newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Santos unions hold fresh talks with Cosipa.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Santos unions hold fresh talks with Cosipa.

text.p: Union officials from the key Brazilian port of Santos presented their fifth cost-cutting plan to steel firm Cosipa at a meeting Tuesday in an on-going effort to solve a labor dispute, an official said.
"Negotiations with Cosipa continue. Today, a new cost-cutting proposal was presented," said Jose Suares Meneses, first secretary of the Santos Stevedores' Union.

The unions and Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) have been in talks since April, when union members staged two strikes at Santos in protest at the steel firm's decision to use its own workers to load and unload at its private terminal.

Meneses said the unions were ignoring recent reported comments by Cosipa chairman Marcus de Araujo Tambasco to the effect that the company planned to hire its own workers instead of using unionized stevedores.
"That was a faux pas and his comments do not reflect the reality, which is that negotiations are continuing," Meneses said.
He could not provide details of the latest cost-cutting proposal, saying negotiators had still not returned from the latest round of talks.
Cosipa will analyze the joint proposal from the three unions involved in the talks and give its reply at the next meeting, scheduled for July 1, a spokeswoman for the company said.
Unions hoped to avoid further damaging strikes, Meneses said.
"We sealed a collective accord with Ultravertil's private terminal last month and consensus prevailed," said Meneses, adding that conditions at Cosipa were similar to those at Ultravertil.
"We hope to arrive at a negotiated solution," he said.
